expected.tagline: A city builder with roads, districts, schools, hospitals, and a city budget. Free, nothing to install, plays on your computer.
expected.description: A city builder with roads, districts, schools, hospitals, and a city budget. Free, nothing to install, plays on your computer.

installSteps.text: Alternatively, download CityRT: build a city on your own or online with friends directly from the official site at https://cityrt.com/en/. Always download from the official source — third-party mirrors of free games are a common malware vector.

Run the downloaded installer and follow the prompts. If Windows SmartScreen warns about an unrecognised publisher, that is normal for open-source projects without a paid code-signing certificate — choose More info, then Run anyway.
Open the downloaded .dmg and drag the app into Applications. On first launch macOS may refuse to open it as unidentified — right-click the app and choose Open to approve it once.
Check your distribution's package manager first, which is usually the easiest route. Otherwise download the AppImage from the official site, mark it executable and run it.

Launch the game and look at the settings menu before your first session — resolution and control defaults are worth checking. CityRT: build a city on your own or online with friends needs roughly small of free disk space.

faq.a: CityRT: build a city on your own or online with friends is a commercial title (Free to play), not a free one.

faq.q: How big is the CityRT: build a city on your own or online with friends download?
faq.a: Check the official site for current download size and system requirements.

faq.q: What platforms does CityRT: build a city on your own or online with friends run on?
Do I need an account to play CityRT: build a city on your own or online with friends?
faq.a: There's no account requirement to play — download and go.

set.tagline: Roads, schools and hospitals are easy to draw. A city budget has other ideas.
set.description: CityRT is a free browser city builder you can play alone or online with friends. Plan roads and districts, provide public services and watch the budget as your settlement grows; no desktop installer is required.

systemRequirements.min: A current desktop web browser with JavaScript enabled and an internet connection. CityRT does not publish CPU, RAM, graphics or disk minimums for its browser game.
systemRequirements.recommended: No separate recommended hardware or browser specification is published by CityRT.

min.notes: Browser game requiring JavaScript. The developer publishes no numerical CPU, RAM, GPU or disk requirements.

recommended.notes: No recommended hardware tier is published; desktop browser support is described on the official site.

set.launcherInstall.note: CityRT runs in a desktop browser with JavaScript. Open its official site to play; there is no Windows installer, Mac DMG or Linux AppImage to download. Online friend play is advertised by CityRT, but PlayBound party handoff is not verified.

qualityBar.verdict: A city builder that places the hard part between the roads you want and the services your budget can afford.

set.longDescription:
CityRT starts in your browser. Open the site and you can begin laying out a city without finding an installer or making room for another desktop client. Roads establish the shape, districts give that shape a purpose, and schools and hospitals turn a promising plan into a place that has to work for its residents. The budget is the quiet troublemaker. Every useful addition has a cost, so expanding a city means deciding what to build now and what can wait.

The official site describes play on your own or online with friends. That makes CityRT an interesting city-building candidate for people who would rather make those decisions together than compare finished maps afterward. Shared construction can turn a practical question into an argument in seconds: extend the road, build the service, or hold onto the money? The site does not publish a player limit or explain the complete invitation flow, so the listing does not promise that a PlayBound party automatically joins the same city. Start from the game's own online options when playing with someone else.

The browser format also sets expectations. CityRT requires JavaScript and is described as a game for a desktop computer; it is not a separately packaged Windows, macOS or Linux application. You can open the same web address on each of those systems in a current browser. There is no local game installer to run, and a PlayBound one-click download would solve a problem the game does not have. An internet connection is part of reaching the site and playing online.

The developer does not publish numerical CPU, memory, graphics or storage requirements. A browser game still puts work on your computer, but assigning it a made-up hardware tier would give the requirement card a confidence it has not earned. Likewise, no physical-controller layout is documented. A city builder may be comfortable with a mouse, yet that says nothing about whether a gamepad works here. Use the site's own controls until a PlayBound Controls profile has been tested. No downloadable dedicated-server package or virtual-LAN setup is documented either.

What catches our eye is the accessibility of the premise: a road, a district, a service, a budget and another person with a different idea of which one should come first. CityRT has the pieces for that sort of collaborative city-building session. We still need hands-on time with the building interface and online join flow before calling the experience verified. For now, it is an easy browser discovery with a clear reason to visit: see whether the city you sketch together can afford to exist.
set.whyWePickedIt: A free browser city builder with an advertised online mode has a low barrier for friends who want to start building together. Roads, public services and budget decisions provide the familiar pressure of the genre. We are keeping it in Draft until the actual play flow, screenshots and party join path are tested.
set.thatOneThing: The first road is free to dream up; the school, hospital and budget meeting arrive right behind it.

installSteps.text: Open cityrt.com/en in a desktop browser with JavaScript enabled. CityRT is free and browser-playable; do not look for an installer.
Start a solo city to learn roads, districts, services and the budget before trying the site's online friend mode.

firstPlaySteps.text: Build a small road network, set out districts and watch what the first services cost before extending the city.

multiplayerGamingSteps.text: CityRT advertises online building with friends. Use the game's own join or invitation flow on its website; PlayBound has not yet verified an automatic party handoff or the maximum players per city.

faq.a: Yes. The official site describes it as free to play in a desktop browser.

faq.q: Do I need to install anything?
faq.a: No. Open the website with JavaScript enabled; there is no verified native installer for Windows, macOS or Linux.
CityRT advertises an online-with-friends mode. Its exact player limit and PlayBound party integration have not yet been verified.
No physical-controller layout or tested PlayBound Controls profile is documented for the browser game.
The developer does not publish CPU, RAM, GPU or storage minimums; use a current JavaScript-capable desktop browser and an internet connection.
